intent.statement: Repair the review-confirmed Disk Steward reliability defects so users receive trustworthy, bounded disk evidence and safe local MCP integrations, without tests disturbing the installed app, without loss of user files or client configuration, and with regression and recovery evidence for the exact repaired candidate.

success_evidence.description: Tests, duplicate launches, and shutdown cannot replace or remove another live application's endpoint or modify real user state.
Published file evidence distinguishes observed presence, validated absence, stale and unavailable coverage across mutation, restart and scope changes.
Monitoring makes measurable bounded progress and recovers database headroom without memory amplification or loss of authoritative current state.
IPC, MCP and client-command execution have bounded work, output, deadlines and effective cancellation/revocation.
All evidence tools export useful bounded and privacy-correct results with actual policy, accurate observation times and typed errors.
Client setup preserves user modifications, is recoverable on partial failure, and distinguishes configuration from real app connectivity and task attribution.
The repaired candidate has isolated CI, regression, scale, lifecycle and upgrade/rollback evidence; release readiness is reported separately from passing unit tests.

constraints: Preserve native Swift/macOS 13, existing tool names where possible, and deliberate version/migration compatibility.
No user-file deletion or delete MCP capability. Preserve live current-state truth and distinguish unknown from absent.
Use isolated fixtures for tests; never open production defaults, safety state, watched roots or sockets in smoke/test mode.
Keep safety budgets and crash-recovery controls; do not raise caps to conceal failure.
Preserve prior completed Pyramid history; existing code is brownfield, not a greenfield project.
Use one focused regression-tested patch per bounded change; no installed-app replacement, configuration migration, commit, push or release without separate user request.
non_goals: Whole-product rewrite or a new filesystem search engine.
Whole-disk scanning or deliberate OOM reproduction on the user's Mac.
General MCP marketplace, remote hosting, EndpointSecurity entitlement expansion or automatic cleanup.
Automatically registering every MCP connection as a coding task.
Guaranteeing zero bugs solely from a passing suite or publishing a release during this repair request.

decisions.question: Which repair path preserves safety and creates demonstrable progress?
decisions.choice: Current baseline: the local correctness candidate builds; 238 isolated tests pass, including native CLI onboarding and bundled-helper checks. Original 213-test evidence and reproduced failures remain historical. Existing fixes must be re-established under brownfield inspections rather than assumed complete; no scale, soak, or release readiness is inferred. Cumulative ladder: Safe testing alongside a running application → Trustworthy current evidence across changes and lifecycle → Useful bounded monitoring progress → Responsive bounded local agent service → Useful and private evidence API → Safe reversible agent onboarding → Regression-assured repair candidate. Each later gate repeats earlier observable safety scenarios on the current candidate.
alternatives: One broad rewrite followed by the existing suite
Raise resource limits and patch only exports
Automate the current unsafe tests and release first
decisions.rationale: Reject the alternatives because they miss reproduced correctness/configuration failures or hide amplification. First rung has actor-visible value: a running application remains queryable while another launch/test executes. Evidence fixes, resource redesign and client configuration changes retain separate rollback and audit boundaries. Early independent fixes can start after test isolation; gate order preserves cumulative proof.

decisions.question: How can necessary repairs proceed without falsely passing shared-asset foundation audits?
decisions.choice: Order acceptance separately from implementation: replace only blanket OUTCOME510 start dependencies with integration-requires, and retain verified CONTRACT510 as a hard prerequisite. Preserve every gate, cumulative outcome dependency and material finding. Scoped fixture work may proceed ahead of foundation audit; no task can pass its audit before OUTCOME510.
alternatives: Mark unresolved broad findings accepted to unblock the foundation
Remove audit or outcome prerequisites
Change plugin enforcement
decisions.rationale: All alternatives weaken assurance or expand product scope. Current isolation/ownership implementation is exercised by64 scoped fixture tests. The revision preserves all7requirements and7gates; source inspection also adds the exact backend/SQLite paths required to fulfill existing TASK541 effective-cancellation acceptance. Existing specific consumed-artifact dependencies remain hard and will be reevaluated only if evidence shows another cycle.

decisions.question: How should the observed endpoint ordering failure enter the existing reliability path?
decisions.choice: Add one bounded ordered-delivery/lifecycle repair under OUTCOME520 and require its evidence at GATE529. Preserve every existing requirement, implementation node, cumulative gate and completed result. Do not hide the failure with a test sleep increase or infer resolution from a later green suite.
alternatives: Only lengthen the endpoint test sleep or retry until green
Fold endpoint queue/lifecycle changes into TASK542 command process ownership
Leave the high-severity endpoint finding unmapped
decisions.rationale: An observed regression plus concrete task-per-event ordering/resource hazard belongs to existing trustworthy evidence and bounded work requirements. Endpoint bridge ownership and callback epochs form one independently testable boundary distinct from subprocess ownership and scanner lifecycle; no new system entitlement or feature is added. Test isolation remains enforced by CONTRACT510; acceptance still depends on OUTCOME510.

decisions.question: How do core scanner timestamp/dirty-fence repairs reach the existing app and public evidence contracts?
decisions.choice: Strengthen the existing TASK522 and TASK552 integration acceptance and required handoff, and GATE559 public interval proof. Extend TASK552 only to the exact provenance/export models and tests required to fulfill existing accurate-evidence intent. Preserve all nodes, seven requirements, seven cumulative gates and completed work; no new product capability or weaker gate.
alternatives: Claim the core change_events correction also fixes exported provenance
Leave the ordinary hint and public timestamp handoffs only in informal progress prose
Introduce a second parallel timestamp workstream with overlapping store/export ownership
decisions.rationale: The two independent code paths are observed, not speculative. Existing lifecycle and public DTO tasks are the earliest actor-visible integration boundaries. Keeping their explicit evidence contracts avoids false completion and competing source ownership; updated impact/inspection records must cover the added attribution/export paths before audit. Scale, rollback, overnight and all prior gate obligations remain.

decisions.question: How do existing lifecycle cancellation guarantees reach the notification side effect?
decisions.choice: Extend TASK522 to its exact delivery adapter and strengthen the existing suspended-callback proof. Serialize the last cancellation check and callback-based native submission on the same main actor as lifecycle transitions. Preserve all nodes, gates, original intent, file-hint acceptance and historical proof.
alternatives: Check cancellation only before calling the async delivery adapter
Permit a suspension between the final check and native submission
Claim already-submitted alerts can be recalled on pause
decisions.rationale: The current adapter ignores cancellation after suspended permission work. Main-actor serialization supplies a precise before/after submission boundary without blocking the main thread during asynchronous system callbacks; fake-center tests avoid real notification permission changes. No core/schema scope added; future receipt design remains separately required within TASK522.

decisions.question: How can ordinary callback receipts fence publication without relying on actor timing?
decisions.choice: Extend existing TASK522 to the exact collector/store/SQLite boundary and one package-owned publication fence. First reproduce receipt-during-preparation in a disposable store and serialize only the final commit with receipt acceptance. Then integrate bounded coalescing, per-root durable invalidation and restart/failure ownership through the concrete app path. Keep AC02 end-to-end proof mandatory.
alternatives: Only enqueue actor invalidation or cancel a task and assume it wins before commit
Hold a callback lock across traversal and full reconciliation
Treat memory-only receipts or discarded overflow as durable evidence
decisions.rationale: These alternatives do not establish the existing invariant or violate bounded-work safety. A final commit permit is an internal synchronization boundary, not a new filesystem snapshot promise; avoid SQLite busy retries under its lock and retain rollback checks. No schema/public API expansion, new framework dependency, or ownership overlap with another active task. All intent requirements and cumulative gates are retained; no whole-task completion from the core subpatch.

decisions.question: How can the bounded storage implementation start when its research prerequisite cannot be verified until that implementation resolves FIND-SCALE?
decisions.choice: Change TASK-531/TASK-532's requires edges to RESEARCH-530 and OUTCOME-520 into integration-requires: the storage tasks may start against the recorded research decision and design candidate, but cannot pass audit until RESEARCH-530 and OUTCOME-520 are verified. No gate, acceptance criterion or finding is weakened.
alternatives: Accept FIND-SCALE for the research rung with an accountable owner so RESEARCH-530 can be audited first; rejected because the finding is real and unresolved and acceptance would be dishonest gating.
Expand RESEARCH-530 into a proof-matrix subtree before implementation; rejected because the matrix cannot be exercised without the production candidate that TASK-531/532 produce.
Leave the graph unchanged; rejected because no storage work can ever start and the reliability intent cannot close.

decisions.question: How can the migration/rollback rehearsal and the soak supervisor be produced when the task that owns them cannot start before the gates they unblock?
decisions.choice: Change TASK-572's requires edge to OUTCOME-560 into integration-requires, exactly as R11 did for the storage tasks: TASK-572 may start its rehearsal tooling and measurements against the current candidate, but cannot pass audit until OUTCOME-560 is verified, and its overnight soak evidence must be re-established on the final candidate at GATE-579. No gate, acceptance criterion, finding or control is weakened; the final-candidate requirement stays in AC-TASK-572-01 and INSPECT-GATE-579-*.
alternatives: Accept FIND-ROLLBACK and FIND-OVERNIGHT for the foundation rungs with an accountable owner; rejected because the rehearsal and soak are real, unperformed controls and acceptance would be dishonest gating.

Move the rollback rehearsal into TASK-511/512 by replan; rejected because those tasks are implemented and their contracts are unchanged, and the rehearsal is acceptance evidence, not an isolation repair.
Leave the graph unchanged; rejected because no audit can ever pass and the reliability intent cannot close.

decisions.question: Is a real-time overnight soak on the final candidate a necessary release gate for this open-source project?
decisions.choice: No. AC-GATE-579-01 and EVREQ-GATE-579-01 now require the scale matrix, the migration/rollback rehearsal and at least one hour of real-time soak evidence on the candidate's product sources; the overnight requirement is removed and TASK-572's summary says 'a real-time soak of at least one hour'. FIND-OVERNIGHT is resolved by the existing scale matrix and the completed real-time soak rather than accepted. No node, edge, rung, gate ownership, finding severity or control is otherwise changed.
alternatives: Keep the overnight requirement and wait for the 8-hour run; rejected by the project owner as unnecessary cost for an open-source release whose long-run feedback comes from users.
Add a development-only real-time watchdog module and review its logs later; rejected by the project owner for the same reason.
Accept FIND-OVERNIGHT with an accountable owner while keeping the criterion; rejected because a criterion nobody intends to meet is dishonest gating.
decisions.rationale: See choice; direction recorded in EV-R13-OPEN-SOURCE-RELEASE-SCOPE.
